title: The £500 Shortfall That Became TransferWise
conflicts: First-year volume: The Next Web (Feb 2012) says about €10m in ~5,500 transfers, Startups.co.uk says £10m; story uses the contemporary euro figure. First funding: Käärmann (BBC 2019) says the first year ran on savings and first funding came from IA Ventures in 2012, but Postimees (2021, citing filings) has Seedcamp investing $70,000 in August 2011; story says 'mostly' savings and calls IA Ventures' $1.3m the first large cheque. Swap currencies: BBC says pounds for kroons; Wise and CNBC say Hinrikus was paid in euros and Käärmann had a euro mortgage in Estonia; Estonian World says a Belgian mortgage (outlier); story says 'Estonian money'. Founding date: company registered 31 March 2010 (Postimees, registry) vs 2011 launch (Wise, BBC); story gives both. Käärmann's employer Deloitte vs PwC; not named.
notes: Episode is the slate's: the swap and the year of building a licensed service from it (2008 bonus to 2012 funding), anchored on Käärmann's BBC 'The Boss' interview (2019) and Postimees's 2021 filing-based history. Funding kept as 'venture' (Seedcamp seed in 2011, IA Ventures in 2012) though the first year ran mostly on savings. Quote stance: affirms.
